name: Ui_SkipPromptWindow_Ctor

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_CtorRows4

name: maybe_Ui_BattleBindWindow_CtorA

The old "BattleCommandWindow" name was wrong: this object is the bind/prompt window, not the command window.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleBindWindow_CtorB
summary: Second variant of the 0x8C-byte "win_bind" window (vtable 0x769940, same seven cleared state words): selected when the battle work byte at +0x4244 is non-zero, i.e. for the other display/UI configuration.
evidence: Same allocation site (Ui_BattleWindow_CreateMainWindow, 0x8C bytes + "win_bind" pane) as 0x003D2260, chosen by the config byte work+0x4244; only the vtable differs. Old name "BattleCommandWindow" was wrong for the same reason as its twin.

Only "which variant" stays open, hence the trailing C.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePartTable_Dtor

Summary now records that it is the deleting form (trailing operator delete).

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B1AC

name: maybe_Battle_QueueActionForGroupUnits
summary: Battle action pass: for every active unit in the four group unit lists (battle work +0x4298) it builds the 0x78-byte action descriptor and queues action 0x54D through Battle_InsertActionSlot, using a descending priority counter from ctx+0x11C.
evidence: Named callee Battle_InsertActionSlot and the four +0x4298 unit lists (stride 0x1C) show this is the battle action queue, not a UI widget queue: the per-unit test is the actor vtable +0x18, exactly like 0x0016C52C (Battle_QueueDefaultActions). The old "Ui_CmdQueue_PushAllWidgets" name came from the descriptor tag constant only.

name: Battle_FinalizeUnitCommands
summary: Second command pass over the party unit list (battle work +0x4260): builds each active unit's action descriptor with 0x00176948/0x001762AC and, for units that report a pending action (vtable +0x1C), commits it through vtable +0x50(unit, 1).
evidence: Named callee group plus the identical unit walk to Battle_QueueDefaultActions (0x0016C52C) and the consumer 0x00174324 (Battle_FinishCommandPhase) which calls this first; the commit call (vtable+0x50 with 1) is what distinguishes it from the queueing pass. Confidence stays at 0.5 because 0x001762AC has no name yet.

name: Battle_FinishCommandPhase
summary: Closes the command phase: confirms the unit commands (0x0016C740), rebuilds every group unit's descriptor, clears the action slots, then moves the battle actor to state 8 or 3 depending on vtable+0x18C and the self[0x4A]/+0xF6 flags. Always returns 1.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Battle_FinalizeUnitCommands and maybe_Battle_ClearActionSlots bracket the body, and the "state 8 on success / 3 on retry" tail is the same state pair the battle sequence uses; the function is reached from the battle update path, so it is the phase-completion step.

name: Battle_QueueDefaultActions
summary: Fallback command pass: for every active party unit that is allowed to act (vtable +0x24), has no forced command (vtable +0x1C == 0) it appends the default action 0x2A to the action list through Battle_InsertActionSlot.
evidence: The named callee Battle_InsertActionSlot with the constant 0x2A and the filter chain (active, allowed, no explicit command) pin the "default action" reading; 0x003212C8 and the other battle managers call it when input or AI produced nothing. Action 0x2A itself is still unidentified, so confidence stops at 0.5.

The exact rule behind the vtable +0x20 call for item type 2 is still unclear, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Actor_ClassifyAnimState
summary: Classifies the actor's current animation phase for the caller: 2 when the actor is in state 0x5C and the current frame is past half of the clip, 3 when it is in state 0x5D with frame > 1, otherwise 1.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_SelectBalloonSlot
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Ui_SelectBalloonSlot(BattleBalloonUi* self, const char* spec, void* slotList, void* units, int unitCount)
summary: Validates a requested balloon-slot selection: counts the occupied slots of the 16-entry array at +0x1C, walks the candidate slots rejecting ones that share the current row or carry state 8/10, then checks the requested count against the number of matching entries and returns 1 when the selection is acceptable.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_GetMemberBalloon
summary: Returns the balloon entry of a member slot when it shares its row with slot 0 and is not in state 8/10; otherwise it clears the cache word and re-resolves the slot through the linked-object helper, returning 0 when the slot index is out of range.
evidence: The two accessors (vtable +0x48/+0x60) and the state tests match the balloon slot array used by 0x001F71A0 and 0x001FA480, so the module is right; "Balloon" is still an inference from those siblings, not from a string or a named caller.

name: maybe_Battle_Actor_CompareConditionFlags

evidence: No caller and no vtable slot, so the use is still inferred; the four symmetric branches over (f_10, type-10 & mask) are a strict weak ordering rather than a plain "flags differ" test, which is why the summary now says ordering. Name kept with maybe_ because the caller side is unknown.

name: Field_Actor_RefreshModelVariant

summary: Refreshes a field actor's model variant: runs the shared scene-object refresh, then selects variant 3 when the actor byte +0x43 is set, variant 2 when the character record's +0xDA bit 0x10 is set, otherwise variant 1.

name: Menu_BuildTargetActorSet

name: Ui_DiveStartWindow_VariantCtor
signature: void Ui_DiveStartWindow_VariantCtor(u32 object, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 in_r3)
summary: Constructor of the dive-start window subclass: chains to Ui_DiveStartWindow_Ctor, installs vtable 0x762C1C and adds the paired member object at +0x35C (secondary vtable 0x75ABE8) with its two 0x18-byte entries.
evidence: The first call is the named Ui_DiveStartWindow_Ctor and vtable 0x762C1C keeps the inherited InitPanes slot, so this really is a subclass ctor of that window; the caller allocates 0x3E0 bytes, registers it and then calls 0x0032BD88 to configure it, which matches. Only "which subclass" is unproven, hence "VariantCtor" at 0.5.

name: Ui_IconCache_FinishLoad
summary: Second stage of an icon load: takes the global icon lock, builds a temporary icon-atlas object on the stack, reads the entry table from the icon bank, and on success clears the shared result block and the completion flags (re-arming the service); returns 1 on success, 0 on failure or when no load is pending.
evidence: Named callees Ui_IconAtlas_Init, Ui_IconAtlas_LoadEntries, Ui_IconAtlas_Release and maybe_Ui_IconCache_EnsureService chain the whole body, and the "load pending" bit is self->f_68 & 1 - the page loader named in the first pass. Confidence 0.55 because the service object 0x7AE4C0 is still unnamed.

name: Ui_IconCache_Close
summary: Closes the icon cache: writes back both pages (0x18C bytes each), drops the record handle, wipes the page structures and the two temporary buffers, and - when the argument is 0 - also releases the service reference and clears the global state flags.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Ui_IconCache_RequestPage and maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReleaseService are the two halves of the body, and the 0x18C/0x318 buffer sizes plus the 0x6262/0x6767 empty-page magic match the page loader 0x0050A100. The argument only selects "flush and release" vs. "flush only".

name: Ui_IconCache_Commit
summary: Commits a pending icon-page operation: reads the 8-byte status (command 0x0A), writes the whole 0x18C page buffer with command 0x01 and reads the status back.
evidence: Both the status read (vtable +8, command 0x0A) and the write (vtable +0x30/+0x34 pair with command 0x01 over 0x18C bytes) appear in the caller set 0x0050B3CC/0x0050B824/0x0050BBD8, i.e. every page operation ends with this; "Commit" describes exactly that.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateCameraAndAnimB
signature: u32 maybe_Field_Actor_UpdateCameraAndAnimB(FieldActor* actor, u32 arg2, int arg3)
summary: Sibling of 0x00591A0C with the same camera-projection + NPC move-animation body; the damaged prologue additionally stores two actor fields, so it is probably a different vfunc of the same class rather than a plain duplicate.
evidence: The tail is identical to 0x00591A0C (Camera_SetupProjection, vtable +0x5C test, Field_NpcUpdateMoveAnimation) but the first instructions are register garbage (unaff_r4/unaff_r6), so the argument list cannot be recovered - maybe_ stays.

name: Field_Actor_UpdateCameraAndAnim
summary: Scene-node virtual: builds the camera projection from the actor's world matrix and, when that and the actor predicate at vtable +0x5C succeed, advances the NPC move animation; returns the animation step result.
evidence: Named callees Camera_SetupProjection, Field_NpcUpdateMoveAnimation and Field_SceneNode_GetPosition cover the whole body, and the same slot is used by the two actor vtables 0x77C230/0x77D8D8; only the "Camera" part is loose (it is the projection the actor is drawn with).

name: Actor_ComputePlayerSide
signature: void Actor_ComputePlayerSide(ActorHandle* handle, unsigned char* out)
summary: Uses the actor's forward vector and the player's position to decide on which side the player stands: writes 1 or 2 into out[1] (0 when the actor cannot be resolved), using the acos of the clamped dot product against the module threshold.
evidence: Named callees Math_QuatToForwardVector, Field_SceneNode_GetPosition and std_Acosf are now identified; the two result values 1/2 with a single threshold angle are the same front/behind split used by the talk/facing code, so the reading holds at 0.5.

name: maybe_Camera_FindVisiblePathEntry
summary: Searches the camera's 16-entry path table for entries whose box contains the reference point and whose path node passes the visibility test, and returns the camera work's path pointer (+0x15CC) once a candidate chain matches.
evidence: The body indexes the per-camera path table and uses the already-named global g_cameraWorkPathEntry for entries without a node, so "visible path entry" is more accurate than the old "visible candidate"; several halt_baddata blocks still cut the return path, so maybe_ and 0.4.

name: maybe_Battle_Action_SelectEffectTarget
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Action_SelectEffectTarget(void* action, u32* units, int unitCount, u32 targetMask)
summary: Scans the candidate target units of an action (array + count) and returns the best matching target handle: it filters by the action's flag mask, checks the field condition/group reference against the acting actor's scenario id and compares the effect transforms through maybe_Battle_ComputeEffectTransform, preferring the lowest record +0x60.
evidence: The new named callees (maybe_Field_Condition_HasActiveRef, maybe_Field_Object_HasActiveGroupRef, maybe_Battle_ComputeEffectTransform) show the function returns a chosen target (local_cc) rather than a boolean, so "ValidateEligibility" was wrong. Which flag bits are tested is still unknown, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Ui_SakusenWindow_CheckCursorAreaFree
summary: Returns 1 when the area reserved for this command entry's cursor does not overlap an already-registered marker: in 3-D mode it tests the actor position against the 3-D markers, in 2-D mode the current target actor's screen rect, and mode 2 runs both tests.
evidence: Sole caller Ui_SakusenWindow_PushCommandForCursor plus the named point/rect tests (maybe_Field_Scene_IsPointInsideBoxSetE / IsPointInsideRectSetC) and the display-mode split via 0x0062AB3C make the whole control flow readable; only the marker registry itself is unnamed.

name: Ui_SlotTable_UpdateSelection
summary: Per-frame slot-selection update: ages the selection timer and applies the pending entry when it expires, then re-picks the active slot for 2-D and/or 3-D mode when the target's screen/world position moved since the last frame.
evidence: Four named callees pin it - maybe_Ui_SlotTable_ApplyEntry, maybe_Ui_SlotTable_Pick2D, maybe_Ui_SlotTable_Pick3D and maybe_Ui_SlotTable_SelectEntry - plus the named overlay position getters for both modes. The two feature bytes +0x37/+0x38 gate the 2-D and 3-D passes.

name: Ui_MenuWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the large menu-window class (vtable 0x76BB8C): releases three embedded widget/list blocks, destroys the nested message page and the 0x414-stride pane arrays, resets the member lists and finalises the object.
evidence: The vtable 0x76BB8C siblings (0x3F34E4/0x3F35B4 in the same table) and the Ui_MessagePage_Dtor + Ui_LayoutRef_Release chain identify the class; it is the non-deleting form (no trailing operator delete), so the name without "Delete" is right.

name: Ui_MenuWindow_DeleteDtor
summary: Deleting destructor for the same menu-window class: runs 0x003F36D8 and frees the block.
evidence: Two-instruction body (call the non-deleting dtor, then operator delete) and it is vtable 0x76BB8C slot 1, immediately next to its non-deleting twin - the classic deleting-destructor slot.

name: maybe_Battle_Unit_UpdateActionState
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Unit_UpdateActionState(BattleUnitView* view, BattleUnit* unit, int* faceData, u32 flags)
summary: Per-frame update of a battle unit's model view: ticks the animation and motion state, and when the animation just finished it looks the unit's face/expression id up in the 0x6400B4 table, resolves the matching part record and plays the SE recorded for it (special id 0x1EA triggers the extra 0x00421C80 call).
evidence: Named callees Anim_UpdateChannels, Model_UpdateMotionState, Sound_PlaySeById and Monster_Model_HandleStateEvent cover most of the body, so the "per-frame unit view update" reading is solid; "ActionState" is still a guess about which state field f_274 is, hence maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B0D4
summary: Child-object factory of one effect-node class (vtable 0x773540, child vtable 0x75B0D4): allocates the 0xAC-byte child, fills the member pair with the parent back-pointer and default-constructs two 0x40-byte sub-objects; OOM is reported through the engine error block at 0x725E4C.
evidence: Same template body as 0x004B1F74 and 0x004B143C in three different effect-node vtables, which confirms the "one factory per node subclass" pattern but not the child class; the field/offset block differs per copy, so the address suffix is kept.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectNodeCreateChild_75B164
summary: Child-object factory of another effect-node class (vtable 0x7767C0, child vtable 0x75B164): allocates the 0xAC-byte child and initialises it with the parent back-pointer and two 0x40-byte sub-objects; depends on the global animation-name block for the OOM report.
evidence: Third copy of the same template (with 0x004721C4 and 0x004B1F74); the OOM path reads the g_actorDefaultAnimName block, which is a detail of this copy only. Child class still unknown, so maybe_.

name: Ui_PokerWindow_InitCardPanel
signature: UiPokerCardPanel* Ui_PokerWindow_InitCardPanel(UiPokerCardPanel* self, void* layout, const void* desc, int user)
summary: Builds one card sub-panel of the poker window: installs vtable 0x777D98, copies the two floats of the shared poker-wheel descriptor into +4/+8 and creates the 0x274-byte tween panel through maybe_Ui_Window_Create4Sub.
evidence: The only caller is Ui_PokerWindow_Ctor, which runs it on the window's +0x18 panel and then keeps the tween object this returns; the named callee maybe_Ui_Window_Create4Sub identifies the created child. The descriptor at 0x72A79C is unnamed, so 0.5.

name: maybe_Camera_RegularShakeKeyData
summary: Not a function: 0x00591204 is a data blob in .rodata - the word 0x0046B5A4, the ASCII map key "ReguralyShake" at 0x00591207 and the float 0xBF800000 at 0x00591218 (checked in the disassembly). The readable C for this entry is the decompiler mis-decoding that data and then folding in the real function that starts at 0x0059121C.
evidence: asm/text/text_00580048.s shows `pop {pc}` ending the previous function at 0x00591200, then the bytes 52 65 67 75 / 72 61 6C 79 / 53 68 61 6B 65 00 ("ReguralyShake") at 0x00591204-0x00591215, then `push {r4, lr}` at 0x0059121C. Nothing branches to 0x00591204, and the readable body assigned to it (params->f_54 = params; unaff_r4->f_15 = ...) is nonsense - so the first pass's "create the shake work" name belongs to 0x0059121C only.

name: maybe_Camera_CreateRegularShakeWorkB
summary: Real implementation of "create the ReguralyShake camera-shake work": allocates 0x94 bytes, constructs it with the named-map key "ReguralyShake" and inserts it into the camera's named map at game work +0x78.
evidence: This is the entry that actually starts with `push {r4, lr}` at 0x0059121C (the neighbouring 0x00591204 is the key string, not code), and it loads its five float parameters from s0-s4 - which is why Ghidra shows in_s0..in_s4 unset. Named callee Camera_RegularShake_Ctor, Container_NamedMap_Insert and the literal key pin the object type; the parameter order is still unknown, so maybe_ at 0.4.

name: Battle_Sequence_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the large (0xDE18-byte) battle-sequence object: runs the sequence base ctor, installs vtable 0x77F02C, sets the four layout scalars (2.0/10.0/1.5/15.0), the 3-row count at +0xDE68 and the -1 / 0xFFFFFC00 sentinels, then resets the member slots.
evidence: Vtable 0x77F02C is the Battle_Sequence class (named siblings Battle_Sequence_Update, _DtorThunk, _DeleteDtor and FieldParty_* live there), and the 0xDE18 size matches the f_D8EC..f_DE09 fields used by 0x005A3FC8/0x005A4F40. The old "Ui_ScreenObject" name was wrong - nothing here is UI; it is also the Squirrel-exposed class built by 0x006C28F0.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateUnitEffectSlot
summary: Pushes the unit's pending effect record to the renderer: when the sequence's record byte +0x29D is set and the 2-D battle-mode flag is on, it forwards the stored position and ids to the renderer call 0x0070FA08.
evidence: The gate (record byte +0x29D plus battle work +0x4244) and the 0x0070FA08 call are readable, but that renderer entry is unnamed, so it is still unclear whether the target is an effect slot or a 2-D unit panel; maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Battle_Sequence_UpdateSlotEffects
summary: Per-frame slot-effect update: resolves the render object referenced by self->f_30 through the global handle table and re-applies its transform/state (func_00234014 or the state-4 path) from the sequence transform; always returns 0 so the sequence keeps running.
evidence: The handle type test (0x20000041) and the two render-state calls are unchanged; func_00234014 and maybe_Gfx_Object_EnterState4 are still only "apply object transform", so the effect-slot wording stays a guess.

name: maybe_Sys_InitCommandRings
signature: void maybe_Sys_InitCommandRings(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int padMask)
summary: Initialises a large session object: pushes 256 command entries into each of two free-list rings, initialises their command/mixing rings (Gfx_InitCommandRing + maybe_Snd_InitMixingState per ring), stores the screen parameters and then configures the pad masks from Input_ReadPadState.
evidence: Two named callees per ring (Gfx_InitCommandRing, maybe_Snd_InitMixingState) show the function builds a graphics AND an audio command ring inside one object - not an input manager. The old "Input_InitManager" name came from the pad-config tail only, which is a small part of the body.

name: maybe_Input_UpdatePadStateThumb
signature: void maybe_Input_UpdatePadStateThumb(int mode, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, u32 arg7, u32 arg8)
summary: Thumb-mode twin of the pad-state mapping: maps the raw button masks onto the three output words and posts them through 0x0010E8D0, with the same 0x00112448/0x00112450 helpers as 0x00108A00.
evidence: Entry is Thumb and registers r4-r11 are read uninitialised (unaff_r*), so the arguments and even the real parameter order are unknown; the constant sequence and the 0x00112448 helper prove only that it is the same pad-mask routine as 0x00108A00.

name: maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker
signature: void maybe_Gfx_CommandListWorker(u32 arg1, u32 b, int c, u32* d, int e, int* f)
summary: Command-list worker: normalises a count modulo 8, validates the list header/count fields and copies command payloads; the decompiler lost most of the flow to a bad instruction, so only the header checks are trustworthy.
evidence: The disassembly range is valid ARM but the decompiler hit bad instruction data, and the entry has no callers (it is reached through a table), so both the name and the signature remain guesses. Nothing new in the merged names changed that.

name: Gfx_ShutdownChannel
summary: Shuts the GPU/display channel down: releases the command slots, closes the kernel handle (svc 0x23), signals and resets the frame event, releases the GPU interrupt and the session, and clears the "channel open" flag. Returns 0 when it actually shut down.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Os_SvcCallChecked, Os_InitEventFlag, maybe_Gfx_ReleaseGpuInterrupt, Gfx_WaitGpuInterrupt, maybe_Gfx_FinalizeSession and Gfx_IpcCmdC0080 cover the body, and the init path Gfx_ShutdownGlobalState (0x001073BC) is its caller. The svc numbers (0x23/0x24) are the handle close/wait pair.

name: Gfx_IsChannelReady
summary: Returns true when the GPU/display channel state machine is in state 4 (ready for a frame).
evidence: The body is exactly `func_0010B9D0() == 4` and the five call sites (0x001051AC, 0x001095A8, 0x0010C2D4, 0x0010C574, 0x00112640) all use it as the "channel open" gate before touching display state.

name: Gfx_SetDisplayEnable
summary: Enables or disables the display: when the request differs from the current channel state it either switches the display to mode 10 (disable) or commits the pending mode (enable).
evidence: Both branches are gated by the now-named Gfx_IsChannelReady and end in Gfx_SetDisplayMode(0,10) / func_0010C534, which is the commit partner of that mode call. The guard byte at state+1 only means "display initialised".

name: maybe_Gfx_SetFrameTimeBudget
summary: Stores the requested frame interval (in ticks) into the global frame-timing record, recomputes the derived 1000/tick value on top of the existing base, and optionally copies the five timing words to the caller.
evidence: The record at 0x7F2644 and the 1000/tick conversion are readable, but the five fields have no named readers yet, so "budget" is still a description rather than a proven meaning; maybe_ stays at 0.45.

name: Snd_SetVoiceLoop
signature: void Snd_SetVoiceLoop(SndVoice * voice, int restart, u32 rate, float startPos)
summary: Programs a voice's sample-loop window: converts the caller's rate and start position into a loop length (at least one sample), stores start/length/end, and switches the voice into the "loop prepared" state; with restart == 0 the existing loop is torn down first.
evidence: The body locks the 4-word loop record (0x0011CBD4), writes f_78/f_7C/f_80/f_84 and drives the state byte f_A1 to 3 or 1 with the f_A3 flag - and all four callers (0x00105584, 0x00105ACE, 0x00105AFC, 0x001EBC68) are the streamed-voice code. The float argument arrives in s0, which is why the signature shows three parameters.

name: Fs_SubmitAsyncTransfer
signature: int Fs_SubmitAsyncTransfer(void* self, void** handle, u32 transfer, u32 extra)
summary: Submits one asynchronous transfer through the object's vtable slot +8 and, when that fails while a handle was produced, releases the half-built handle (0x00114CF0); returns the transfer status.
evidence: The body is a thin wrapper whose only extra behaviour is the failure cleanup, and all four callers (0x00105584 handle-table sweep, 0x00105ACE, 0x00105AFC, 0x001EBC68) are on the async I/O command path. Confidence 0.5 because the vtable slot +8 implementation is unnamed.

name: Pack_ApplyToLoadedHandles
summary: Pushes a value into every live handle of a streamed slot - the two buffers at +0x34/+0x3C, the pack-backed one at +0x40 and each 0x14-byte record of the bitmap table at +0x7C - but only when the corresponding pack record reports type 2.
evidence: The shared type-2 test (0x0011BAC0 record lookup) is repeated for each handle and the bitmap walk honours the 0x18 skip bits, which pins this as the "apply to all loaded handles" helper; the same four callers as the voice/stream code use it. The applied value's meaning is unknown, so 0.5.

name: std_RingBuffer_Push
signature: void std_RingBuffer_Push(BufferQueue* queue, unsigned int value)
summary: Blocking push into a bounded producer ring: waits on the "not full" semaphore while the write index equals the capacity, stores the value, advances the write index and signals the consumer; a separate counter guards concurrent callers.
evidence: The body uses only Os_LockMonitor / Os_SemaphoreAcquire / Os_SemaphoreRelease on a plain index/capacity record - there is no sound-specific call, so the "Snd_" prefix of the first pass was a guess from its neighbours. Generic container code uses the std_ prefix, hence the new name.

name: Ui_Object_ReleaseLists
summary: Releases a UI object that owns several intrusive lists: frees the four resource handles at +4/+8/+0xC/+0x10, then walks the lists at +0x14, +0x20 and +0x2C, calling each element's virtual destructor (slot +4) or releasing its resource handle.
evidence: Named caller Ui_CompositeWindow_ReleaseHandles and the named Pack_ReleaseHandleEntry calls fix the "release a composite window's member lists" reading; the twin 0x001BB8F0 is the same walk without the four leading handles.

name: Ui_EntryList_FindByIdList
signature: int* Ui_EntryList_FindByIdList(UiEntryTable* self, u32 key, u32 id, u32 scratch)
summary: Looks an entry up by numeric id: resolves a two-word key through the object's id list (+0x24), searches the shared hash map with that key and releases the temporary key reference before returning the hit.
evidence: Both halves are now named - maybe_Ui_EntryList_ResolveByIdList and Container_HashMap_FindByKey - and the wrapper is byte-identical to 0x001BC138 except for the list it resolves against (+0x24 vs +0x18), which is exactly what the names claim.

name: Ui_Window_ReleaseLists
summary: Bulk teardown of a large window: clears the 0x18-stride and 0xC-stride record vectors (releasing each element), frees the SMART-pointer vector at +0x298, releases the five embedded members, resets the page pool and sets the "nothing selected" sentinel 0xFF at +0x398.
evidence: Named callees Event_ClearEffectsAndHandles, maybe_Event_ResetState, maybe_Svc_ReleaseMemoryBlock, maybe_Container_DtorWithArrays and Ui_LayoutAnim_Reset walk through the whole body, and the 0xFF sentinel matches 0x002555F4.

name: Ui_EntryList_FindByKeyList
signature: int* Ui_EntryList_FindByKeyList(UiEntryTable* self, u32 key, u32 id, u32 scratch)
summary: Same id lookup as 0x001BBF20 but resolved against the object's primary key list (+0x18) instead of the id list (+0x24): builds the two-word key, searches the shared hash map and releases the temporary reference.
evidence: Byte-identical wrapper to 0x001BBF20 apart from maybe_Ui_EntryList_ResolveByKeyList vs. ResolveByIdList, and its caller 0x004D2538 uses both variants - so the two names now describe a real distinction observed in the code.

name: Ui_HandleSet_DtorAndUnlink
summary: Full destructor of a handle-set object: installs vtable 0x7596D4, releases the four handles at +4..+0x10, runs the list teardown 0x001BB8F0, unlinks the four remaining intrusive lists and releases the nested handles, returning the base pointer.
evidence: The named callee maybe_Ui_RowList_ReleaseItems is the list teardown, and the four unlink pairs are the standard "unlink self from list" idiom; the caller 0x00605B1C sits in the release helper of the factory that creates it.

name: maybe_Container_RbTree_Dtor
summary: Destructor of an object that owns a red-black tree plus a fixed table: destroys the 0x21-entry 0x10-stride table at -0x2CC, then erases every tree node at -0x2E0 using the tree's successor helpers, empties the root and unlinks the object before freeing it.
evidence: The walk uses func_00115358/func_00115390 (tree successor/left-most) with std_RbTree_EraseNode, i.e. a std::map/std::set - not an intrusive list as the old name said. The enclosing class is still unknown, so maybe_ and 0.45.

name: Ui_HandleSet_IsReady
signature: bool Ui_HandleSet_IsReady(UiHandleSet* self, u32 arg2, u32 b, u32 c)
summary: Returns true only when every resource the object references is loaded: it validates the four handles at +4/+8/+0xC/+0x10 (object state < 4) and every entry of the two child lists, rejecting the first one that is still loading.
evidence: The four unrolled probes and the two list walks use the global handle table at 0x7BA2D0 with the same "< 4" state test; the caller 0x006038F4 and the sibling 0x001BC67C (the matching destructor) fix the class as the composite-window handle set.

name: maybe_Ui_BigView_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a very large (~0xD78-byte) object: runs its base teardown, unlinks two list nodes, destroys four fixed arrays (12 entries plus three blocks of 10) and releases the trailing handle before freeing.
evidence: The base teardown is the named maybe_Field_ShutdownSlots, which weakens the "Ui" attribution of the first pass; the four std_destroy_range calls use the same 0x6F43A0 element destructor, so the array sizes are certain but the owning class is not.

name: Ui_PanelMessage_Dtor
signature: void* Ui_PanelMessage_Dtor(UiPanelMessageWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Destructor of the panel message window: destroys the sub-window at +0xF0, releases the ten text objects at +0xE0..+0xE9 through the UI heap, then unwinds the ~20 embedded member blocks and frees the object.
evidence: Vtable 0x75A570 and the ten func_0021F8B8(heap, member) calls match the member layout seeded by 0x001E0028/0x001E0258, and the callee is the named Ui_GetCore. It is the deleting form (ends in operator delete) even though the old name omits it.

name: Ui_PrizeWindow_Dtor
signature: void* Ui_PrizeWindow_Dtor(UiPrizeWindow* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Destructor of the prize window: releases the three gfx/text objects at +0x38/+0x3C/+0x40 through the UI heap, then releases the member ref at +0xD0, tears down the sub-object and frees the window.
evidence: The three func_0021F8B8(Ui_GetCore(...), member) calls and the member chain match the layout created by 0x001E61B8; vtable and offsets are consistent with the prize-window family.

name: Ui_Window_DestroyLists
summary: Destroys a window's dynamic containers: calls the first virtual of every 0x14-byte record in the vector at +0x3F0, releases the 0xC-stride handle vector and the 0x18-stride record vector, and releases the trailing smart handles.
evidence: The same two vectors (0x18-stride records, 0xC-stride handles) are cleared by the named maybe_Ui_Window_ReleaseLists (0x002543E4), and the empty sentinel 0x782690 is written to +0x3DC - so both functions operate on the same window class.

name: maybe_Ui_Object_Dtor
summary: Destructor of a small object that owns one smart handle: installs its vtable, releases the handle at +0x10 (with the handle-table validity test), unlinks the node and frees the block.
evidence: The vtable itself is still only named maybe_g_nodeDtorTable by an earlier batch, so the class cannot be confirmed as a UI object; the body (handle release + unlink + operator delete) is fully readable, hence 0.45 with maybe_.

name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseHandleChain4
summary: Vtable/delete helper for a composite object that owns four nested reference-counted handles: releases them in sequence and returns the owner base pointer (the last release minus 4).
evidence: The chain of four Pack_ReleaseHandle calls with -8 offsets is certain, but neither the owning class nor the caller is named, and "Pack_" is only the name of the release helper it calls; maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Pack_ReleaseHandleChain1
summary: Single-handle variant of 0x00120408: releases one nested reference-counted handle and returns the owner base (release result minus 4).
evidence: Two instructions (Pack_ReleaseHandle, then return -4) with no caller name; the "Chain1" wording is purely structural and the owning class is unknown.

name: Ui_RowList_ReleaseItems
summary: Unlinks and destroys every node of the three intrusive lists owned by the object (heads at +0x14/+0x18, +0x20/+0x24, +0x2C/+0x30): the first two call each node's virtual destructor, the third frees the enclosing object from the embedded node at +0xC.
evidence: It is called by the named full destructor 0x001BC67C (maybe_Ui_HandleSet_DtorAndUnlink) and is its no-handles twin, so the "row list" reading and the three-list layout are consistent; the first two lists really are polymorphic nodes.

name: Anim2D_Dtor
summary: Destructor of the 2D animation player: releases the reference-counted channel block at +0x9FC (the field the binder 0x002B3128 installs) and then tears down the class at 0x003A8200, which frees its 0x19 x 0x50 animation slots.
evidence: The +0x9FC reference release matches exactly what 0x002B3128 stores there, and the 0x003A8200 teardown is the 0x19*0x50 slot owner - so the class is the same one. The current symbol for 0x003A8200 (maybe_Ui_WorldMapMarker_Dtor) is probably a misnomer from an earlier batch.

name: maybe_Ui_DetachAndReleaseMembers
signature: int maybe_Ui_DetachAndReleaseMembers(void* self, u32 value, DetachTarget* target)
summary: Stores value into target+8 and then releases the three reference-counted members at self+0x14, +0xC and +4 in that order, returning self (the release helper returns its argument).
evidence: Only three Pack_ReleaseHandle calls and one store; no caller and no vtable, so the "detach" part is an inference. The field order and the +8 store are now stated exactly so a later pass can match them.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemInfoWindow_SubDtor
summary: Destructor of a member/sub-object class of the item-info window family (vtable 0x761E58): deletes the owned object at +0x13C, releases the reference at +0x138, tears down the 0x128-byte sub-object and frees the block.
evidence: The existing symbol Ui_ItemInfoWindow_Dtor already names the window class itself at 0x0045287C (vtable 0x771428, neighbour Ui_ItemInfoWindow_Open 0x2F6A44), so this second dtor in the same 0x2F6xxx family must belong to one of its members - hence the rename from the first pass's window-level name. The member teardown (0x0021DD60 on a 0x128 block) is still unnamed, so maybe_.

name: Container_DtorWithArrays
summary: Destructor of a container that owns two arrays: installs its vtable, runs the class cleanup, releases every 8-byte entry (handle at +4) and destroys every 0xC-byte entry (Effect_List_DestroyAll + handle release), then drops the container's own reference.
evidence: The named callee Effect_List_DestroyAll identifies what the 0xC array holds, and the two loop bounds (self[0x19]..self[0x1A] stride 8, self[8]..self[9] stride 0xC) are the arrays the same class fills elsewhere; the class itself is only "Container", hence 0.5.

name: maybe_Handle_ResolveOwner
summary: Releases two nested reference-counted handles from an implicit this and returns the owning object (last release minus 4); reached only through a data pointer, never called directly.
evidence: Two Pack_ReleaseHandle calls and a pointer adjustment, nothing else: the "Os_HandleResolveOwner" prefix of the first pass claimed an OS/handle-table meaning that the body does not show, so the family prefix is dropped and the name stays maybe_.

name: Monster_ModelInstance_DtorB
summary: Destructor of the second monster-model instance class (vtable 0x780A20): tears down the two embedded animation/effect blocks, then releases the two trailing pack handles and frees the instance.
evidence: Vtable 0x780A20 and the member block layout are unchanged from the first pass, but the callees are now known to be the animation-slot teardown func_003F76F0 and the handle/alloc releases maybe_Ui_Widget_ReleaseAlloc, which confirms it is a model-instance destructor rather than a UI one.

name: maybe_Fs_ResourceHandle_Init
summary: Stores the given value into the object and releases the nested handle at +0x3C, returning the address 0x3C bytes before the released node (the owner base).
evidence: Two statements; the -0x3C offset matches the handle field used by 0x005F9138/0x005F9428, so the family is consistent, but no caller or vtable pins whether this is an init or a detach.

name: maybe_Pack_ResourceChain_Dtor
summary: Destructor helper for a resource chain: releases the handle at +0x58 and the two nodes before it, rewrites the shared vtable 0x77F6C4 and returns the owner base (0x3C before the last node).
evidence: The three release calls and the vtable write are readable, but the class owning this chain is unnamed and the base-0x3C convention is shared with 0x005F951C, so it stays a structural name.

name: maybe_Effect_Emitter_ReadVariantB
summary: Reads a record row into the object's f_2C8.. block: checks the id against the bag's flag set (+0x24A98) with 0x0066B3B0, copies the four u16 fields of the record, and marks the id as seen (0x006125F0); returns 1 when the row existed.
evidence: The data path is now clear (bag flag check, record read, mark-seen), so this is a record-read helper rather than necessarily an effect emitter; the object class is still only the first-pass guess, hence maybe_ and a summary that states the mechanics.

name: Script_MakeNameHandleByIndex
summary: Builds a name handle for the script context's current entry: reads the index at context+0xB4+0x14, resolves the record through 0x0063E070 (only when the index is below 0x5AE) and turns either the first or second u16 of that record into a handle via maybe_Script_MakeNameHandle; falls back to a literal handle when no record exists.
evidence: The named callee maybe_Script_MakeNameHandle is the actual builder and the 0x5AE bound matches the record count used by the script message tables; only the "which of the two u16" semantics is unnamed.

name: maybe_Actor_UpdateEquipStateByte
summary: Recomputes a unit's equipment-state byte at +0xDE0E: resolves the party member of the unit's slot-0 child, tests the member's equipped item category (slot 1, category 6 clears the flag) and forces 0 when the unit's owner object has +0x307 clear.
evidence: The new named callees (maybe_Item_SlotIsCategory6, func_006292F0 equipped id, Item_LookupRecord category at +0x29) confirm the item-category path; what the byte +0xDE0E is consumed by remains unknown, so maybe_.

name: Battle_IsInputMode0B
summary: Predicate used by the battle command input: returns 1 when the battle input-mode byte (+0x4208) equals 0x0B and the queried action id is 0 or 7 (id 6 is explicitly excluded).
evidence: The byte compared with 0x0B lives at battle work +0x4208 (work->0x5C + 0x4208), not in field code, so the "Field_" prefix of the first pass was wrong; the action-id test accepts 0/7 and excludes 6, which is the "no command / cancel" pair.

name: Model_Actor_ResetAttachmentParts
summary: Resets the actor model's three attachment effect parts: for each of the handles at +0x708/+0x70C/+0x710 it resolves the part and calls Gfx_EffectPart_ResetToDefault(part, 1), then detaches attachment slots 2, 3 and 4.
evidence: The body contains no sound call at all - the three calls are Gfx_EffectPart_ResetToDefault on effect parts resolved from handle fields - so "StopAttachmentSounds" was wrong. The three func_004EDA08(self+0x700, 2/3/4) calls are the slot detach, matching the sibling 0x00378704.

name: maybe_Model_ResetSingleAttachmentPart
summary: Reduced variant of 0x00377AF8: clears the state byte at +0x271, resets the single effect part held at +0x70C and detaches attachment slots 2, 3 and 4.
evidence: Same +0x700 attachment block and the same Gfx_EffectPart_ResetToDefault(part, 1) / func_004EDA08(slot) calls as the actor version, so this object is a model/actor, not a "Ui_Window" as the first pass guessed. Only one part handle is reset here, which is why the name says "single".

name: Battle_ActionSequence_BeginTurn
signature: void Battle_ActionSequence_BeginTurn(BattleActionSequence* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Starts a turn: clears the participant counter, takes the action count from the sequence record (+0x1FB), applies the x3 multi-hit rule when the actor has the 0xA0 flag, and picks the first acting slot with the battle RNG (func_001CA474).
evidence: The field triple +0x377B/+0x377D/+0x377E is the same one the named maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_AdvanceTurn/GetPendingActionCount use, and the x3 rule duplicates 0x003C38EC - so this is the "begin" counterpart of the advance step.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnSlotEffectA
summary: Spawns the effect attached to the current unit's first slot id (record +0x2C2): resolves the unit actor, builds the 0x5C-byte parameter block on the stack and creates the effect through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance, storing the handle at self[slot + 0x2E79].
evidence: Named callee Effect_FindOrCreateInstance plus the paired spawner 0x003C90A8 (same body, id +0x2C4, colour f_2A5) make the pattern certain; the slot-id fields are still only known by offset, hence A/B and 0.5.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnSlotEffectB
summary: Second per-slot effect spawner: same as 0x003C8F74 but for the unit record's +0x2C4 id and colour byte f_2A5, storing the handle at self[slot + 0x2E89].
evidence: Identical call sequence to 0x003C8F74 with only the id/colour/store offsets changed, and both end in the named Effect_FindOrCreateInstance - so these are two parallel effect slots of the same battle UI context.

name: maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_AdvanceTurn
summary: Advances the turn cursor: bumps the participant counter at +0x377D, re-selects the acting slot (0x003C3414 when the all-ready flag is set, otherwise the next entry) and stores it at +0x377B, then fetches the actor for the new slot.
evidence: The counter logic matches the named BeginTurn/RunCommands siblings, but the tail that resolves the actor is decompiled as bad instructions (coprocessor_*/halt_baddata), so the argument and return conventions cannot be verified.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_AreActionsReady
summary: Returns 1 when every planned action slot is either empty or still resolvable through the handle table (and the four balloon/spawn flags are satisfied), 0 while something is still pending; on the way it drives the four member-balloon spawners for the pending slots.
evidence: The named callees maybe_Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloonB/C/D and the 16-slot handle validation (0x007B4D68 table) cover the body, and the function is called by the battle sequence update just before RunCommands.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_RunCommands
summary: Runs the queued commands of a round: builds the processed-index list, keeps dispatching the current actor's commands (ProcessActorCommand) while the pending count allows it, then advances the turn and repeats for every acting actor of the round.
evidence: All three callees are now named - maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_GetPendingActionCount, _ProcessActorCommand and _AdvanceTurn - so the loop is fully understood; only the f_DDF4/f_DDF8 actor-count fields are still positional.

name: Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTalkMembers
summary: Applies the talk-member state to every party member while the sequence is in the talk sub-mode (record +0x1F8 == 2 and +0x1F9 in 1..3), calling maybe_FieldParty_UpdateTalkMemberState for each member.
evidence: The loop is a direct call of the named maybe_FieldParty_UpdateTalkMemberState over the member count, and the gate bytes match the sub-mode constants used by the talk code elsewhere in this batch.

name: Battle_Ui_AttachActionSprite
signature: void Battle_Ui_AttachActionSprite(BattleActionSeq* self, int recordId, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Attaches the sprite named by a battle action record: resolves the record through Game_GetDataManager (type 0x0063E05C), and when it carries a sprite id (f_5A != -1) calls the owner's attach slot vtable+0x40 with f_5A-0x7F.
evidence: Sole caller Battle_ActionSequence_Update and the companion 0x004D2DA0 (same guard, no -0x7F bias) show this is the action-effect sprite range; the sprite table itself is unnamed, hence 0.5.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneObjArray_Ctor
summary: Default-constructs five 0x0C-byte records at the given address with element ctor 0x0022AEA4; the rest of the original body was lost.
evidence: Only one statement survives, and the four callers (0x3702FC/0x3A26CC/0x3A2ABC/0x3AD38C) are scene-object initialisers - not enough to confirm the "Ui_SceneObj" class, so maybe_ at 0.35 with the exact element count now stated.

name: maybe_Battle_DispatchEventToUnits
signature: void maybe_Battle_DispatchEventToUnits(void* self, u32 event, u32 argument, void* callback)
summary: Per-unit dispatch helper: when the battle work's +0x4254 list state is not 7, it walks every unit of the +0x4270 list, builds a 0xB0-byte event record for it and calls the handler selected from the object's callback table (via the type returned by 0x0017... on unit+0x8F0).
evidence: The two lists are the battle unit lists (+0x4254/+0x4270, stride 0x1C), not a UI widget list, and the per-unit call is a table dispatch on the unit's own vtable - so "Ui_CmdQueue_PushAllWidgets" was wrong. The exact event type is unnamed, hence maybe_.

name: Battle_QueueCommandMenuEntries
summary: Builds the command entries the battle menu consumes: for every valid unit of the party list, the all-unit list and the four group lists it pushes action 0x28 (row) and 0x33 (group header) with a descending priority starting at 100 (0x557/0x55C for the group variant).
evidence: The named maybe_Ui_CmdQueue_PushEntry is the only queue call, and the three passes plus the separate group action ids (0x557/0x55C) show exactly how each character/monster row reaches the command list. Only the action ids remain unexplained, so 0.55.

name: Battle_QueueFirstUnitAction
summary: Finds the first active unit in the four group lists and queues action 0x55E for it through a small descriptor, returning immediately after the first match.
evidence: The four-list walk and the immediate return are explicit, and the queue call is the named maybe_Ui_CmdQueue_PushEntry; the descriptor tail (0xB word) is unknown, but the "first unit, one action" reading is solid.

name: maybe_Battle_ClearTargets
signature: void maybe_Battle_ClearTargets(Battle * battle, u32 arg2, u32 * action)
summary: Invokes the action object's reset slot (vtable +0x80) and then default-constructs four 8-byte target descriptors on the stack; most of the body was lost because the call does not return to the decompiler.
evidence: Only two statements survive, so "ClearTargets" is still an inference from the target-descriptor count (4 x 8 bytes, element ctor 0x005906C0); the caller Battle_Update does not disambiguate it.

name: Battle_TargetMarker_ClearLists
summary: Clears the target-marker object's three working blocks (two 0xD0-byte arrays and a 0x59-byte table) and, when asked, the four state words at +0x1A0..+0x1AC.
evidence: The three block sizes and the optional state clear are exact, the sole caller is Battle_Update, and the object is the same marker list the battle target UI uses; 0.5 because the class itself has no named vtable.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionScene
summary: Presentation state machine for the current battle action: driven by the state word at +0x134 (0xB0F/0xB43/0xB47 sentinels) it waits for the acting unit to become idle, spawns the hit effect at the unit's node, picks the model/animation by unit id and advances the camera/scene state; returns 1 while frames are still needed.
evidence: The named callees Actor_IsIdleAndQueueEmpty, maybe_Ui_PopupEntry_SpawnUnitEffect and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance identify the "wait, spawn, advance" phases, but the state constants and the f_E4/f_F0 fields are not named, so maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName
signature: void Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName(GfxEffectPart* self, GfxNode* source, const char* name, const unsigned* params)
summary: Binds a named effect part: shares the source node's resource block, copies the part name (fixed 31-char string) into the part, resolves the node id for that name on the source model, copies the 12-word parameter block and resets the 4-word default block.
evidence: The field block it fills (f_174 source, f_17C..f_198 name, f_19C node id, f_1A0..f_1CC params, f_1D0..f_1D8 vector, f_1DC flag) is exactly what Gfx_EffectPart_UpdateTransform (0x005F79E0) consumes, and the named callees Model_GetNodeIdByName / std_FixedString31_Ctor cover the body.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloon
signature: void Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloon(u32 owner, int textId, BattleUnit* member, int useAnchor)
summary: Spawns the balloon effect for one member: remaps the text id to 0x46B when the member is in the item state (0x79), computes the anchor from the member model node and creates the 2-D effect instance through Effect_FindOrCreateInstance.
evidence: The named callee Effect_FindOrCreateInstance targets the 2-D effect manager (work+0x60), and the 0x79 state remap matches 0x001F8010/0x001F5D14; "balloon" is the project's established word for these text-carrying effects.

name: Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloonEx
signature: void Battle_Ui_SpawnMemberBalloonEx(BattleBalloonUi* self, int textId, int memberId, int* out)
summary: Variant of 0x001F7E10 that walks all sixteen member slots, averages/uses their anchor positions and spawns the balloon effect for each valid member when the battle work's +0x4244 flag is set.
evidence: Same remap and Effect_FindOrCreateInstance call as 0x001F7E10, plus the 16-slot loop and the +0x4244 gate - so "Ex" means the all-slots variant.

name: maybe_Effect_SpawnOrientedInstance
summary: Spawns an effect instance from a request that carries a locator/actor reference plus a direction: derives an orthonormal basis (two normalised vectors and their cross products) from the source transform, fills the 0xE0-byte parameter block and calls Effect_FindOrCreateInstance with the resulting matrix.
evidence: The reconstruction is still marked as a recovered entry point with no direct callers, and the request struct is only positional; the basis maths and the final Effect_FindOrCreateInstance call are clear, so "oriented instance" holds at 0.45.

name: Gfx_EffectPart_UpdateTransform
summary: Per-frame transform update of a bound effect part: composes the part's offset with its source node/cached node id, converts the resulting matrix to scale/quaternion/position (+0x88..+0xA4) and smooths the position offset (+0x1D0) with the part's parameter matrix (f_1A0).
evidence: The field block matches Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName (0x005F56A0) one for one - f_174 source, f_19C cached node id, f_1A0 parameter matrix, f_1D0 smoothed offset, f_1DC frame counter - so this is the effect-part updater, not a trail renderer as the first pass guessed. The sole caller 0x003F44E4 copies the resulting transform from +0x88.

name: maybe_Model_UpdateNamedNodeAndId
summary: Debug/validation hook: when the global switch at 0x7A3168 is on it resets the model's "N_ALL" node to the default transform and re-registers the model's two record ids; when the second switch is on it re-applies the render object at f_30C.
evidence: The string literal "N_ALL" and the two global switches are the only anchors; whether this is a debug aid or a mandatory refresh depends on how those switches are set at runtime, which is not visible in the readable C, so maybe_.

name: Battle_Effect_UpdateLinkSegment_2
summary: Recomputes one segment of a link/rope effect between two actors: resolves the attachment node on both actors, transforms the node offsets with the actor matrices, normalises the segment vector and hands position+orientation to the shared link updater.
evidence: The named callees maybe_Gfx_ModelAttach_SetLocatorPairById and maybe_Battle_Effect_UpdateLinkSegment are the two halves of the body, and the structure mirrors 0x004EC4A0 exactly (the "2" suffix only marks the twin). The +0x5D7 parameter block is still positional, hence 0.5.

name: Gfx_Node_ApplyBoneMatrixToChildren
summary: Builds the world matrix of a weapon/attachment bone (quaternion + translation scaled by the model's bone scale) and writes it, together with its normal matrix, into every child render object of the node list.
evidence: The body resolves the bone record by name (Model_GetNodeIdByName + 0x002D6AC4 bone table), then writes the f_1A0..f_220 block of each child - the render object's world and normal matrices. The named sibling constructors around 0x468xxx place it in the model/render code.

name: Ui_SortWidgetsByPriority
summary: Distributes up to three widgets into the slot table by their type id (400 / 0x360 / 0x361), then sorts the remaining widgets by the key returned from their vtable +0x68 (insertion sort below 0x3C elements, introsort above) and writes the sorted order into the output slots.
evidence: The sort helpers it calls are the already-named Ui_SortWidgetsByPriorityMerge, Ui_SortWidgetsByPriorityMergeB and Ui_MergeWidgetsByPriority, so "ByPriority" is the family's established term and "ByLayer" was a misnomer; the key really comes from vtable +0x68 with a per-slot flag byte.

name: maybe_Battle_UpdateActionAnim
summary: Advances the per-action transform pair (self+0x35C / self+0x304, interpolated by Event_ActorModels_Update) and, when the battle scene is active, switches the current actor to state 8 (animation finished). Always returns 1.
evidence: The named callee Event_ActorModels_Update and the +0x4320/+0x404 checks are readable, but f_E4 and f_304/f_35C are positional, so whether this is the action animation or the scene camera pair is still open; maybe_ at 0.45.

name: Map_PlaceObject
summary: Places an object on the level grid: computes the two transforms with Map_ComputeObjectTransform, ensures the shared map service exists and inserts the instance through Map_AddInstance, storing the resulting node at object+0x31C.
evidence: All three callees are named (Map_ComputeObjectTransform, Map_AddInstance and the shared context bootstrap), and the caller set is the ten field placement sites - the whole body is explained.
